..
Issued at 136 PM EDT Sat Oct 10 2026

Pattern Synopsis/Forecast:

Temperatures more reminiscent of late summer across the Northwoods 
early this afternoon, driven by gusty south winds and plenty of 
sunshine. Current readings spiking up into the 70s for most... 
running a good 10 or more degrees above specific normal values for 
today's date. Apex of upper level ridge responsible for the above 
continues to mature...part of a larger long-wave amplification 
process driven by deepening western NOAM centered troughing and post-
tropical storm "Isaias" rotating up into the Tennessee River Valley.

Overhead ridging will remain in control through Monday, forcing a 
quick northeast deflection of the remains of "Isaias" tonight into 
Sunday through the lower Ohio Valley and up into the mid-Atlantic 
States. Northern extent of ridge axis does look to gradually break 
down heading through the middle of the week as north-displaced 
northern stream flow becomes a bit more aggressive across southern 
Canada. 

Primary Forecast Concerns:

Temperature trends and addressing any shower potential through the 
period.

Details: 

Confidence continues to increase that deepest moisture plume and 
attendant rains with Isaias will remain off to our southeast tonight 
into Sunday...with northern lower Michigan likely just seeing some 
increasing high and mid level clouds. Again, biggest story remains 
the unseasonably mild conditions into Monday. Those clouds and a bit 
less agressive low level mechanical mixing should keep temperatures 
on Sunday just a smidge cooler than those observed today, but still 
looking at widespread highs in the lower to middle 70s. Weak cold 
front does begin to drop south into the northern reaches of our 
footprint on Monday, keeping much of northern lower in the warm 
sector through the day. Thermal progs easily support highs well up 
into the 70s for most south of the big bridge Monday. Wouldn't be 
terribly surprised if someone down near Saginaw Bay makes a run at 
80. More clouds and increasing chances for showers across eastern 
upper will keep readings up that way in the 60s (still well above 
normal).

Front will work slowly south across the area Monday night into 
Tuesday morning, with its southern descent perhaps slowed further by 
weak low pressure riding east along it. Shower coverage looks to 
increase along and just behind this front with that passing low, 
with moisture profiles perhaps helped along by remnant tropical 
moisture from what is now tropical storm Rachel off the coast of 
Baja California (Rachel is expected to race northeast, making 
landfall in the northern part of that Mexico state later tonight). 
High end rain chances are warranted by later Monday night into early 
Tuesday. Early indications most areas will receive a quarter inch or 
less of much needed rains. However, given the potential for that 
enhanced tropical moisture plume to cross overhead, could easily see 
some locally higher totals by later Tuesday morning. 

Front looks to clear our area to the south on Tuesday, with post-
frontal north winds bringing temperatures back to near normal levels 
in the 50s and lower 60s. Questions abound to what happens for the 
rest of the week, with uncertainty specifically centered on just how 
aggressive late week troughing becomes across the Great Lakes. 
Deterministic guidance has most definitely diverged on this 
potential, with even vast differences within the intra-model 
ensemble suite themselves. While it still appears temperatures 
should trend cooler from current conditions, just how cold they 
become and any additional shower chances will be entirely predicated 
on exactly how the long-wave pattern unfolds. Unfortunately, that is 
an exceedingly low confidence portion of the forecast at this time. 
Of course, still plenty of time to work out those details in the 
coming days. Stay tuned.
